_about: Photo-derived materials (CLAUDE.md rule 16). The textures in scripts/v2/materials/<slug>/ are made FROM the owner's photographs with the photo's light divided out; factor x texture (linear) = the base colour on the light-rig scale. Texture coordinates are made at tile build time from position and normal: on a wall u runs along the wall and v up, elsewhere plan x/z; both in metres / repeat_m.

filter.why: measured (v2-shimmer, S 250 m): plain trilinear left the textured wall softer than the truth (+0.02); anisotropy 8 + bias -0.15 gives -0.03 with shimmer 0.00 (main 0.05). The window-frame coverage fade was dropped: it only made the frames softer than the truth (+0.01) and did not lower shimmer.

anchor.why: one number to overrule: the first build's cast-stone level (luminance) is kept. Hue from IMG_0998, the photo whose light is neutral: its walls face the lawn, trees and a concrete walk, and its concrete walk (taken as neutral) reads only 4 % green / 9 % blue cool, which is divided out (linear g x0.917, b x0.822). IMG_1031 is NOT used for hue: its sky is as neutral as IMG_0998's (b/r 1.05 vs 1.08, same lens, 4 minutes apart, both dry), but its walls face an enclosed court of red brick paving and brick walls, whose warm bounce light tints every wall there (the paving reads b/r 0.58); its matched light carries that bounce (wb set from the stone, a known material).

fade._why: rule 15: blades, bars and frame are finer than a pixel from about 60 m; as they go below a pixel, they AND the dark panel behind them go over to the same colour, the screen's coverage-weighted mean (32 % blade, 68 % dark gap, from the counted pitches), so the far screen is one steady tone at the truth's average: no flicker, not darker or softer than the truth
